# ethereum-optimism/infra Weekly Report (Jul 12 - 18, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on hardening the project's containerization strategy and refining the dispute game lifecycle within the OP Stack. A primary theme was achieving production readiness for APKO images by ensuring parity with legacy Docker configurations and fixing critical argument bugs for `proxyd` and `op-ufm`. Significant architectural discussions also took place regarding the simplification of the `op-challenger` and the potential retirement of pre-Regolith testing suites to streamline the `op-e2e` system tests.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Containerization & CI/CD Optimization
Efforts this week were centered on transitioning to APKO for image builds to improve security and reproducibility while maintaining functional parity with existing Docker workflows.
*   **APKO Production Readiness:** A critical fix was implemented to address parity gaps between APKO and Docker images. This specifically resolved a bug in default configuration arguments for `proxyd` and `op-ufm`, ensuring these images are viable for production promotion ([#668](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/668)).
*   **Workflow Maintenance:** The APKO factory workflow pin was updated to the latest merged commit, ensuring the CI/CD pipeline utilizes the most recent configurations and security patches ([#667](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/667)).

### Protocol & Dispute Game Refinement
Technical discussions advanced the logic behind how the OP Stack handles finalized states and cross-layer interactions.
*   **Dispute Game Lifecycle:** Developers explored simplifying `op-challenger`'s handling of `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame`. A key technical requirement identified is the need for the challenger to `close()` games after finalization to update the anchor state registry.
*   **Interface Standardization:** To support the above, there is an active proposal to add `closeGame()` to the generic `IDisputeGame` interface to handle games that resolve to `DEFENDER_WINS` but currently lack a standardized closure method.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **RPC Configuration:** The proposal to change the default RPC binding address from `0.0.0.0` to `127.0.0.1` was closed as "not planned." The team determined that `0.0.0.0` remains the correct default for containerized environments to ensure reachability, noting that security is maintained via opt-in privileged APIs ([#16487](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/16487)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Integration Test Flakiness:** The `reth-optimism-node` integration tests are experiencing non-deterministic `SIGSEGV` errors during teardown. The issue is suspected to be a race condition in the payload builder service's runtime teardown ([#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20973)).
*   **Legacy Test Retirement:** Discussions are ongoing regarding the removal of pre-Regolith tests. This is a prerequisite for deleting `ELKindOpGeth` in system tests, moving the project toward a requirement for Bedrock/Regolith co-activation ([#21451](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21451)).
*   **Kona Soundness:** The review of host game input and witness generation for `Kona` was reopened to address lingering TODOs regarding request retries in the `OPSuccinctDataFetcher` ([#18430](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18430)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by deep technical synchronization between the infrastructure and protocol teams. There is a concerted effort to keep the `op-revm` crate in sync with upstream `revm` and `reth` releases to support upcoming milestones like Glamsterdam in Hardhat 3 ([#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21069)). The interaction across issues [#21678](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21678) and [#21708](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21708) highlights a highly coordinated approach to refactoring the `op-challenger` logic, ensuring that architectural changes are reflected across the `IDisputeGame` interfaces.
